title: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Korea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Korea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for South Korea: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in South Korea (the Republic of Korea). Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - covering medical certification, civil registration and the One-Stop Inheritance Service, funeral or repatriation procedures, pension and health insurance notifications, and succession and inheritance tax filings in South Korea.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital or medical clinic in South Korea, the attending physician, dentist, or Korean medicine doctor issues the official Death Certificate (Samang Jindanseo) in accordance with the Medical Service Act and guidelines of the Ministry of Health and Welfare [6]. Request at least 7 to 10 original signed copies of the Samang Jindanseo, as separate originals are required by the hospital mortuary, municipal crematorium, civil registry, banks, and insurance institutions [2][6].
  • Deaths at home or outside a medical facility: If your family member died at home or outside a hospital, a physician must examine the body and issue a Post-Mortem Examination Certificate (Siche Geom-anseo) [6].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the cause of death is unnatural, sudden, or unknown, notify the Korean National Police Agency (112) or emergency services (119) immediately. The police and a public prosecutor oversee the forensic examination (sometimes through the National Forensic Service) and issue a prosecutor's certificate approving release of the body before funeral or cremation arrangements can proceed [1][6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (Within 1 Month)
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Act on the Registration, etc. of Family Relationships administered by the Supreme Court of Korea, cohabiting relatives (or non-cohabiting relatives, the householder, or the head of the facility where the death occurred) must file the Report of Death (Samang Singoseo) within 1 month of learning of the death [1][2]. Late filing triggers an administrative fine (gwataeryo) [1].
  • Where and how to file: Submit the Report of Death, the original Samang Jindanseo or Siche Geom-anseo, and the informant's identification at any local community service centre (Jumin Senteo / Haengjeong Bokji Senteo at the Si, Gun, Gu, Eup, Myeon, or Dong level) or electronically via the Electronic Family Registration System of the Supreme Court of Korea [1][2]. Registration automatically cancels the deceased's Resident Registration Number and updates the Family Relations Register (Gajok Gwangye Deungnokbu) [1].
  • One-Stop Inheritance Integrated Service (Ansim Sangsok): At the exact same time you file the Report of Death at the community service centre (or within 1 year of the end of the month of death via the Government24 Portal), submit an application for the One-Stop Inheritance Integrated Service (Ansim Sangsok) [2]. This single application queries the deceased's bank accounts, insurance policies, debts, national and local taxes, real estate, vehicles, and pension records across participating institutions [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Hospital funeral halls (Jangnyesikjang) and cremation: In South Korea, funerals typically follow a 3-day custom (Sam-il-jang) held at a licensed hospital funeral hall (Jangnyesikjang) regulated under the Act on Funeral Services, etc. overseen by the Ministry of Health and Welfare [6]. Reservations for municipal crematoria are booked nationwide through the official e-Haneul Funeral Information System upon presentation of the medical death certificate [6].
  • International repatriation of a foreign citizen: If the deceased was a foreign national, report the death to the Ministry of Justice (Korea Immigration Service) to surrender the Residence Card (formerly Alien Registration Card) and notify the deceased's embassy in Seoul [2]. International transport of human remains requires an English or translated medical death certificate, an embalming and non-contagious disease certificate, and quarantine clearance at Incheon International Airport [6].
  • Apostille legalisation: South Korea is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. For Korean death certificates or Family Relations Certificates (Gajok Gwangye Jeungmyeongseo) used abroad, obtain an Apostille electronically or through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Overseas Koreans Agency, or through the Supreme Court of Korea for court and notarial records [1][2].

steps.title: Notify National Pension, Health Insurance, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• National Pension Service survivor benefits: If the deceased contributed to the national pension scheme or received an old-age or disability pension, surviving dependents (spouse, children under age 25, parents, grandchildren, or grandparents meeting statutory dependency criteria) should file a claim with the National Pension Service for a monthly Survivor Pension (Yujok Yeongeum), a Lump-Sum Refund, or a Lump-Sum Death Payment [3]. Claims must be filed within 5 years of the date of death [3].
  • National Health Insurance Service and funeral expenses: Once the death is registered, civil registry data is transmitted to the National Health Insurance Service to terminate health insurance eligibility and settle any outstanding co-payments or refundable medical expense ceilings [4]. Check whether the deceased was covered by industrial accident compensation (Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service) or public official pension schemes [3][4].
  • Banking and Financial Supervisory Service lookup: Use the results from the Ansim Sangsok inquiry via the Government24 Portal (and the Financial Supervisory Service inherited financial transaction lookup) to identify all accounts, credit cards, loans, and insurance contracts before requesting account closure or transfer [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Inheritance Tax Filings
steps.html:
• Statutory succession shares and wills: Under the Civil Act of South Korea, if the deceased left no valid will (holographic, notarial, secret, recorded, or dictated will meeting strict statutory formalities), the estate passes to statutory heirs in rank order: (1) direct descendants and spouse, (2) direct ascendants and spouse, (3) siblings, and (4) collateral relatives within the fourth degree [1]. The surviving spouse receives a 50% premium over the share of each heir in the same rank [1].
  • Crucial 3-month deadline for renunciation or qualified acceptance: Under Korean civil law, heirs inherit both assets and liabilities automatically unless they file a petition with the Family Court under the Supreme Court of Korea within 3 months of learning of the commencement of inheritance [1]. If debts may exceed assets, heirs must apply to the Family Court within that 3-month window for either Renunciation of Inheritance (Sangsok Pogi) or Qualified Acceptance (Hanjeong Seung-in, which caps liability at the value of inherited assets) [1].
  • Inheritance tax deadlines with the National Tax Service: An Inheritance Tax return (Sangsokse) must be filed with the National Tax Service within 6 months from the last day of the month in which the death occurred [5]. If either the deceased or any heir is domiciled outside South Korea, the statutory filing deadline with the National Tax Service is extended to 9 months from the last day of the month of death [5].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your exact situation, was your family member a Korean citizen or a foreign resident, and are there any estate debts or heirs living outside South Korea that affect the 3-month Family Court and 6-to-9-month tax deadlines?

prefillQuestion: A family member has died in South Korea. We need an overview of the main official steps and authorities in South Korea for civil death registration, funeral arrangements, survivor benefits, and estate probate or succession requirements.

contacts.name: Supreme Court of Korea
contacts.note: Oversees the Family Relations Registration system for death reports and Family Court petitions for qualified acceptance or renunciation of inheritance.

contacts.name: Government24 Portal
contacts.note: National e-government portal administering civil certificates and the One-Stop Inheritance Integrated Service (Ansim Sangsok) for deceased persons' assets and debts.

contacts.name: National Pension Service
contacts.note: Administers Survivor Pension (Yujok Yeongeum), Lump-Sum Refund, and Lump-Sum Death Payment claims for surviving dependents.

contacts.name: National Tax Service
contacts.note: National tax authority responsible for Inheritance Tax (Sangsokse) filings due within 6 months (or 9 months for non-resident cases) from the end of the month of death.
